Hi Daniel — looping in a bit more technical context.

Short answers up front:
- OpenAI-compat: Redwood provides OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints and SDK wrappers. For most workloads the swap is literally a change of base_url + key; we include sample code (attached: openai-compat-sample-code.zip).
- Behavioral diffs: differences typically come from tokenization and model checkpoint variants. Our plan: run the exact prompt set against both endpoints, collect token-level diffs, and surface actionable mappings (prompt tweaks, stop sequence adjustments, temperature tuning).
- Metrics: we'll capture p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost estimate using your expected traffic profile.

Proposed concrete tests (we can execute within 5 business days of getting the prompt set & test creds):
1) Smoke test (20 prompts): ensure compatibility and streaming behavior
2) SDK integration test (small service sim): swap client, run 1k requests, check for errors
3) Full prompt diff run (120 prompts): collect outputs, token counts, and a behavioral diff report

I'll run the tests on a Redwood Dedicated node to match your latency profile; if you prefer hosted, we can do that as well.

See attached quick comparison (redwood-vs-hypercloud-comparison.pdf) — it highlights where we've seen the biggest differences in other financial customers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
